questions.q: Iron wool practical. (a) Give the % oxygen from start 50.0 cm³, end 39.6 cm³ [2]. (b) Explain why the water level rises [2]. (c) Suggest why the answer is slightly below 21% [1]. (d) Name the main gas left and explain why it remains [2].
questions.a: (a) 10.4 ÷ 50.0 × 100 = 20.8% (2); (b) iron reacts with oxygen (1), reducing gas volume so water is pushed in (1); (c) not all oxygen used/not left long enough (1); (d) nitrogen (1); unreactive (1)
questions.model: Teacher sets out (a): oxygen used = 50.0 - 39.6 = 10.4 cm³.

questions.q: Explain why rising CO₂ levels may cause climate change.
questions.a: CO₂ absorbs infrared radiation emitted by the Earth (1), warming the atmosphere (enhanced greenhouse effect) (1)

questions.q: Why is the copper method faster than the iron wool method?
questions.a: Heated copper reacts quickly with oxygen; rusting at room temperature is slow.

questions.q: Write the balanced equation for the thermal decomposition of copper(II) carbonate.
questions.model: Heat breaks it down into the metal oxide and carbon dioxide: CuCO₃ → CuO + CO₂. Atoms: Cu 1, C 1, O 3 both sides.

questions.q: Describe the reaction of sulfur with oxygen.
questions.a: Burns with a blue flame (1) forming sulfur dioxide (1)
